title: A hanging chain, flipped, is the perfect arch
body: A flexible chain hangs in a catenary, pure compression's mirror: flip it and the same curve stands as an arch carrying its weight without bending. Hooke announced it in 1675 as an anagram; Gaudi later designed with hanging-chain models, literally inverting gravity into architecture. Galileo had guessed parabola for the chain and was gracefully wrong.
